answer: On a breezy night, a lone lantern cast a faint glow over the vast network, where a zephyr of activity signaled the emergence of new identities. As the kernel of the system hummed along, a subtle defense mechanism kicked in, one that made it costly for attackers to create multiple fake identities. By chaining previous work to each new identity, the system forced attackers to continually diverge from their old patterns, making it increasingly difficult to maintain the illusion of separate entities.
